entry.title: Registry Maintenance tooling (v0.9.0 unchanged): Maintenance workflows added to the registry, none of which changes a dataset, a grade, a status or a licence ...
entry.content:
6 Sep 2026.

Maintenance workflows added to the registry, none of which changes a dataset, a grade, a status or a licence class: a harvester that queries Europe PMC, OpenAlex and Crossref for every instrument and writes a candidate artefact for a person to screen; a weekly watcher that hashes the visible text of every licence page the registry cites and opens an issue when one changes; a monthly watcher that checks every cited DOI for retraction and update notices; and a tripwire that accepts a monthly cycle only when the run artefact is complete over the full inventory and named by an issue the workflow itself opened. Harvest runs are configured to write an artefact and open or update a review issue. Licence and retraction watchers upload their results and raise an issue when they report a change, signal or incomplete run. The tripwire opens an issue if it cannot verify the monthly cycle and no issue for that cycle already exists. A first dry run over 12 July to 5 September 2026 is recorded as an engineering result, not as evidence about retrieval.

entry.title: Registry v0.9.0: Reconciliation of the fifth review pass, of v0.8.0 and scoped to the changes 1.5 made, before first ...
entry.content:
3 Sep 2026.

Reconciliation of the fifth review pass, of v0.8.0 and scoped to the changes 1.5 made, before first publication; the check's verdict was fit to publish with one grade to move first, and its three findings and two notes were all taken. Rubric v1.6: the norm rule is read as written, so a High grade on populations, languages and norms rests on a study that states a norm, cut-off, prevalence or reference value and not on a word that matches the test; section 10 says that precondition evidence sits only on a High cell or a High previous block. One grade moved, COPSOQ III populations, languages and norms High to Moderate (the entry that met the rule names a shared-variance figure in the Czech screening version; the study that carries norms in substance states no value in its abstract, and the cell returns to High when those values are read from the full text, first on the check list). European Working Conditions Survey internal consistency changes status from well-established to thin, grade unchanged at Low. The K10 criterion-validity judgement is corrected in one clause (the two developer studies are two designs, not one programme), grade unchanged. The WHO-5 populations cell notes that its one norm-bearing entry is a cut-off validated in diabetes patients and holds on its working-adult entries. One statistic gains a population clause with its value unchanged. All 420 DOIs resolved on the conformance date. Schema 0.7 unchanged. Every changed cell keeps its 1.5 values in previous. Logged as correction C-0009.

entry.title: Registry v0.8.0: Reconciliation of the fourth review pass, of v0.7.0, before first publication; the check's verdict was fit to ...
entry.content:
3 Sep 2026.

Reconciliation of the fourth review pass, of v0.7.0, before first publication; the check's verdict was fit to publish and its ten findings were non-blocking, every one of them taken. Rubric v1.5: a High grade on populations, languages and norms rests on at least one counted study carrying a norm, cut-off, prevalence or explicitly reported reference value, and the build tests it (every current cell holds); criterion validity is two lists, so a correlation or regression coefficient counts only against organisational outcomes; the rubric's statistic lists and the machine check are reconciled in both directions, a comma bounds a clause, and one entry's statistic is reworded with its value unchanged; section 10 gains a row for every check the build already ran. One grade moved, European Working Conditions Survey internal consistency Moderate to Low (no reliability coefficient of the record's own; the embedded WHO-5's alpha belongs to the WHO-5 record). The K10 criterion-validity judgement is rewritten, grade unchanged. All 420 DOIs resolved on the conformance date. Schema 0.7 unchanged. Correction C-0008. Fifth pass, scoped to the diff, pending before the noindex lift.

entry.title: Registry v0.7.0: Reconciliation of the third review pass, of v0.6.0, before first publication; the check found no grade ...
entry.content:
2 Sep 2026.

Reconciliation of the third review pass, of v0.6.0, before first publication; the check found no grade demonstrably wrong. Rubric v1.4: the High precondition names the statistics of each property and the build tests every cited study against its own property's list (nine studies leave the tables on four cells; every one of those cells keeps two or more and stays High); high_basis is renamed precondition_evidence, the studies that meet the precondition, and a cell that drops from High keeps that evidence in its history; internal consistency on item sets and derived indices is stated; a flag descriptor may name a population by the survey, trial or organisation that sampled it; a direct reason lists a working-adult sample first; the rule that borrowed evidence never grades High is now checked; every rule names its check and the unchecked ones are listed. One High grade drops to Moderate (k10 criterion validity against a reference standard, on a credible published disagreement, the rater's judgement written on the cell), two internal-consistency cells become Not-applicable (wpai, fcs-maps), two population tags and two evidence forms are corrected. All 420 DOIs resolved. Schema 0.7: eight-field previous blocks. Logged as correction C-0007 with the rubric 1.3 values kept on each changed cell. No fresh literature search: as-of dates unchanged.

entry.title: Registry v0.6.0: Reconciliation of the second review pass, of v0.5.0, before first publication.
entry.content:
2 Sep 2026.

Reconciliation of the second review pass, of v0.5.0, before first publication. Rubric v1.3: the evidence-form rule recodes a cell to the form its findings attribute instead of capping its grade, so a cell is mixed only where the findings name two forms claim by claim; a High grade needs two cited studies with a sample size and a statistic of the property graded, and on a population-sensitive property at least one of them in a working-adult or general-population sample, with every cited study tagged by population; criterion validity against a reference standard joins the population-sensitive properties (diagnostic accuracy depends on the sample); every flag descriptor names a population. One Moderate returns to High (k10 internal consistency, capped in v0.5.0 on a coding error), five High cells drop to Moderate, four single-item invariance cells and one derived-index structure cell become Not-applicable, three flags move, 24 cells are recoded off mixed, 29 cited studies leave the High-basis tables for want of a statistic of the property. Schema 0.6: population on High-basis entries, two absence types, seven-field previous blocks, structured abstract contradictions. One gate module now runs in both the migration and the site build. All logged as correction C-0006 with the rubric 1.2 values kept on each changed cell. No fresh literature search: as-of dates unchanged.

entry.title: Registry v0.5.0: Reconciliation of the review pass of v0.4.0, before first publication.
entry.content:
2 Sep 2026.

Reconciliation of the review pass of v0.4.0, before first publication. Rubric v1.2: the indirectness flag has three values (direct, general, indirect), each cell states the studies its flag rests on, a grade never moves because a flag moved, and a High grade needs at least two cited studies with a sample size and a statistic, listed on the cell. The six C-0004 grade moves are reversed and six further High cells drop to Moderate (three for want of the numbers, two for indirect evidence on a population-sensitive property, one for a mixed cell that names no second form); 49 flags change; six criterion cells that had been graded on a reference standard the construct does not have become Absent (category error); four not-applicable cells become Absent and one Absent cell becomes not-applicable. Every Absent or Not-applicable cell names its absence type and carries no flag. Schema 0.5: indirectness_basis, absence_type, high_basis, a corresponds-with relation for single items whose only published link to an instrument is a correlation, and a generated integrity block. The site build now fails on any cell that breaks these rules. All logged as correction C-0005 with the rubric 1.1 values kept on each changed cell. No fresh literature search: as-of dates unchanged.

entry.title: Registry v0.4.0: Purpose reset before first publication.
entry.content:
2 Sep 2026.

Purpose reset before first publication. The registry's purpose is stated: the open synthesis of the published evidence on instruments used to measure workplace health and wellbeing, scope the whole field by construct, the first 27 instruments stage one. Rubric v1.1: indirectness is defined by population type, never by country or language; every cell re-read, 92 flags changed and 6 grades moved (all upward, all occupational instruments), logged as correction C-0004 with the rubric 1.0 values kept on each cell. Schema 0.4: every indirectness flag carries its reason; relations on every record link single items and short forms to the multi-item instruments they were validated against, each citing its study; new single-item measures page. Freeze dated from first publication. Search venues and strings published on the methods page. No fresh literature search: as-of dates unchanged.

entry.title: Registry v0.3.0: Schema 0.3.
entry.content:
2 Sep 2026.

Schema 0.3. Every graded cell now carries an evidence state (assessed, assessed_absent, not_assessed, not_applicable), the rubric version it was graded under, the date its literature was last searched, the date its grade was last confirmed by a rater, and a review-due flag. Grading rubric v1.0 published and linked from every cell. Licence figures replaced by a licence class for employer or vendor use, with archived copies of steward pages linked on each record. Single-rater disclosure recorded in the dataset: grades and statuses frozen from 1 Sep 2026 until two named non-employee raters join. Errata list and right-of-reply policy added. Steward-product disclosure field added, not yet populated. No grades moved. Migration script published beside the dataset.
